tier2.summary:
INCOMPLETE
  ✗ pytest runs green from a clean checkout against a live ephemeral DuckBrain namespace: Committed HEAD d2dcad3 is FLAKY, not reliably green. Command: `python3 -m pytest tests/test_auger.py -q -p no:cacheprovider` (pytest 9.1.1; live DuckBrain at http://127.0.0.1:3000 confirmed reachable, 200 on GET /api/namespaces). Isolated clean runs gave '27 passed in 23.57s' and '27 passed in 59.55s', but also '1 failed, 26 passed in 18.69s' and '1 failed, 26 passed in 39.98s'. Decisive reproduction: two concurrent runs of the same suite BOTH returned '1 failed, 26 passed', each failing tests/test_auger.py:524 test_no_test_namespace_survives_the_suite with 'AssertionError: test namespaces were left behind: {api: [auger-pytest-4fa9b730f450, auger-pytest-05310a25e0fb], disk: [...]}'. Root cause: tests/conftest.py:112-121 leftovers() scans the GLOBAL 'auger-pytest-' prefix across the API registry and ~/duckbrain/namespaces instead of only the names this session created, so a sibling process's live in-flight namespaces are misreported as leaks. tests/gate.sh:23 runs this exact suite with `|| exit 1`, so the gate is red under concurrency. A fix exists only as an UNCOMMITTED working-tree patch (git diff tests/ adds scope=CREATED to leftovers()); it is not part of the deliverable.
  ✓ the suite asserts on STORED ROWS (re-read via the API), not only on stdout: tests/test_auger.py: test_start_stores_the_project_row_and_embeds_the_seed re-reads row(ns,'project',...) via auger.select and asserts p['seed']==seed; test_answer_writes_every_decision_field_to_the_row asserts project_id/domain/chosen/why_not/confidence/status/evidence_key off the stored decision row; test_answer_makes_the_chosen_option_the_only_active_one asserts stored option active flags [True,False]; test_toggle_flips_the_stored_active_flags re-reads option_flags(ns) before/after and asserts the flags flipped; test_dump_config_does_not_mutate_the_stored_rows compares before/after stored option flags; test_dump_config_names_the_contradiction_with_the_recorded_reason reads why_not off the row rather than hardcoding; test_status_counts_the_stored_rows asserts len(rows(ns,'decision',...))==2; test_patch_reporting_zero_updates_leaves_the_flag_unchanged asserts option_flags(ns)['D-001-O1'] is True after a broken patch. Helpers rows()/row()/option_flags() all call auger.select (API read).
  ✓ the namespace is torn down even when a test fails: tests/conftest.py:159-169 ns_created fixture uses try/yield/finally; the finally calls teardown_namespace(ns) which issues DELETE /api/namespaces/<ns> AND shutil.rmtree(ns_path(ns)), then re-verifies via api_namespaces(). Empirically proven: injected tests/test_teardown_proof.py with a test using the `ns` fixture that then raises AssertionError; result '1 failed in 0.07s' (FAILED test_deliberate_failure_after_using_ns, ns='auger-pytest-83fe0a28c53f'), and post-run checks showed disk '(none)' and api '[]' — the namespace was fully removed despite the failure. Proof file removed afterward.
  ✓ a deliberately broken verb fails exactly one named test: tests/test_auger.py:441-505 test_a_broken_verb_fails_exactly_one_named_test writes a child suite (BROKEN_VERB_SUITE) of four verb tests with `auger.patch = lambda *a, **k: {'updated': 0}` (toggle write broken) and runs it via subprocess with its own conftest copy and `-c pytest-child.ini`. Actual run of `pytest tests/test_auger.py::test_a_broken_verb_fails_exactly_one_named_test -q -s` produced: 'F...  [100%]', 'FAILED test_broken_f3b15f46.py::test_alpha_toggle_flips_the_stored_flag - Ass...', '1 failed, 3 passed in 0.58s', failure message 'AssertionError: the toggle reported success but wrote nothing', and the outer test '1 passed in 0.74s'. Exactly one named failure, three passed.
Three of four criteria are met and empirically proven, but criterion 1 fails: the committed suite is flaky because conftest.leftovers() scans the global auger-pytest- prefix, so concurrent runs of the same suite misreport each other's live namespaces as leaks (reproduced: both concurrent runs returned '1 failed, 26 passed'), and the fix exists only as an uncommitted working-tree patch.
